record.original_question: Does every bounded linear operator T on a separable Hilbert space H have a nontrivial closed invariant subspace? Here, an invariant subspace of T is a subspace M ⊂ H such that T(M) ⊆ M.

evidence.quote: The third open problem that the semigroup W is related to is the Invariant Subspace Problem (ISP), which asks: Does every bounded linear operator T on a separable Hilbert space H have a nontrivial closed invariant subspace?
An invariant subspace of T is a subspace M ⊂ H such that T (M) ⊆ M.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space, and let B(H) denote the algebra of bounded linear operators on H. A closed subspace M ⊆ H is called invariant under T ∈ B(H) if T(M) ⊆ M, and is called nontrivial if M ≠ {0} and M ≠ H.

Question: Does every bounded linear operator T ∈ B(H) admit a nontrivial closed invariant subspace?
artifact.status_search_result: The Invariant Subspace Problem for separable Hilbert spaces remains one of the most famous open problems in operator theory. Counterexamples are known on certain Banach spaces (Enflo, Read), but the Hilbert space case is still unresolved as of 2026. A 2023 preprint by Per Enflo claiming a solution has not been generally accepted/verified by the community.

status_evidence.title: Invariant subspace problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In the field of mathematics known as functional analysis, the invariant subspace problem is a partially unresolved problem asking whether every bounded operator on a complex Banach space sends some non-trivial closed subspace to itself. The problem is open for separable Hilbert spaces.
status_evidence.claim: ISP remains open for separable Hilbert spaces.
